limitations: No detector-rule catalog entry or implementation was provided for the label DeprecatedApiSpec, so its complete matching algorithm is unknown.
A type-level warning does not identify the exact member, overload, arguments, preference XML resource, or storage mode involved.
The finding does not prove that the reference is reachable or executed at runtime.
The finding alone cannot establish migration correctness, preference-data compatibility, or a concrete attacker-controlled security impact.
predicates: A program element resolves to, or invokes a member through, android.preference.PreferenceManager.
The resolved Android platform class is documented as deprecated in API level 29.
The reference is distinguishable from androidx.preference.PreferenceManager by qualified name, import resolution, or equivalent symbol metadata.
detector_semantics.claim: A finding claims use of the documented deprecated Android platform API android.preference.PreferenceManager; Android documentation directs developers to the AndroidX Preference Library.

unknowns: No independently verified detector-rule implementation or rule catalog entry defines the exact matching algorithm associated with the DeprecatedApiSpec label.
It is unresolved whether findings are emitted for every legacy type import/reference, only for calls, or only for a subset of PreferenceManager members.
It is unresolved whether target SDK, minimum SDK, dependency version, source set, suppression, or generated-code exclusions affect reporting.
The particular legacy PreferenceManager member used by an individual finding is not established by the representative type-level message.
Whether existing preference files, keys, XML resources, storage choices, and lifecycle integrations remain behaviorally compatible after migration is not established.
It is unresolved whether the observed deprecated use has security relevance beyond the indirect maintenance and compatibility concern described by CWE-477.

documented_behavior: android.preference.PreferenceManager is the legacy Android platform class used to help create Preference hierarchies from activities or XML.
Android documents android.preference.PreferenceManager as deprecated in API level 29 and directs developers to the AndroidX Preference Library for consistent behavior across devices.

androidx.preference.PreferenceManager is the AndroidX library class used to help create Preference hierarchies; its getDefaultSharedPreferences(Context) method returns the default preference-framework SharedPreferences instance for the supplied context.
preconditions: A source-level deprecated-API finding requires evidence that the legacy fully qualified type resolves to android.preference.PreferenceManager rather than an identically named type.
If getDefaultSharedPreferences(Context) is invoked, its documented AndroidX signature requires a non-null Android Context.
Use of AndroidX APIs requires the corresponding AndroidX Preference library to be available to the build and packaged application.
unknowns: The representative finding does not establish which legacy PreferenceManager member is used.
The consulted documentation does not establish that every legacy-platform use can be mechanically substituted with an AndroidX call.
Preference-data, XML, storage, and lifecycle compatibility require application-specific evidence and testing.

events.condition: Observed when an import, type reference, constructor reference, or member-call receiver/declaration resolves to android.preference.PreferenceManager. A textual match alone is insufficient when symbol resolution is available.
events.name: legacy_preference_manager_reference_observed

events.condition: Satisfied only when the resolved referenced API is android.preference.PreferenceManager, which Android documents as deprecated in API level 29. A call-shaped expression without a resolved owner does not satisfy this predicate.
events.name: deprecated_api_predicate_satisfied

events.condition: Observed when a reference resolves to androidx.preference.PreferenceManager. This is replacement-family evidence only; it neither satisfies the legacy-platform deprecation predicate nor proves complete migration or compatibility.
events.name: androidx_preference_manager_reference_observed

important_note: DeprecatedApiSpec is a concern label, not a governed API type and not a CrySL rule. This context establishes static evidence of use of a documented deprecated Android platform API only; it does not establish exploitability, runtime reachability, runtime failure, or a behavior-preserving migration.
forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: Do not infer that DeprecatedApiSpec is a Java, Android, AndroidX, CrySL, or third-party API type.
Do not infer a specific invoked member, overload, argument value, preference XML resource, or storage mode from a type-level deprecation message.
Do not infer that a use of android.preference.PreferenceManager is unreachable, harmless, exploitable, or runtime-failing merely because it is deprecated.
Do not infer that replacing an import with androidx.preference.PreferenceManager preserves preference keys, XML interpretation, storage behavior, lifecycle behavior, or UI behavior.
Do not infer that an unqualified PreferenceManager identifier denotes the platform class without import, qualification, or symbol-resolution evidence.
Do not infer that AndroidX use is a complete remediation without dependency, source, build, and supported-device compatibility evidence.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: The evidence does not establish runtime execution, API removal, data loss, privilege compromise, information disclosure, or another concrete security impact.
security_semantics.detector_claim: The detector identifies use of a documented deprecated API; it does not establish an equivalent runtime security claim.

compatibility: Build-dependency and import-resolution evidence for the AndroidX Preference artifact.
Preference XML, preference-key, storage-location, and data-migration tests before claiming behavioral equivalence.
Testing across the application's supported Android API levels before claiming cross-device compatibility.
runtime: A packaged-artifact reference and execution evidence before claiming that the deprecated path is reachable at runtime.
Device/API-level testing before claiming runtime behavior, failures, or behavioral differences.
A concrete affected operation plus supporting exploit or impact evidence before claiming a runtime security impact.
source_level: A resolved import, fully qualified reference, compiler symbol, or bytecode owner identifying android.preference.PreferenceManager.
Applicable Android SDK documentation or API metadata showing deprecation of that platform class.
If asserting a replacement, resolved evidence for androidx.preference.PreferenceManager rather than a same-named class from another library.

name: DeprecatedApiSpec
semantic_scope: For every finding, the detector concern is source or bytecode use resolving to the deprecated Android platform type android.preference.PreferenceManager, including use of that type as the owner of a member invocation. It excludes similarly named APIs, an API type named DeprecatedApiSpec, and proof of a security exploit.
known_false_positive_shapes: An unqualified PreferenceManager token that resolves to androidx.preference.PreferenceManager or another non-platform type rather than android.preference.PreferenceManager.
A comment, documentation block, string literal, reflection string, or generated text containing android.preference.PreferenceManager when detection is lexical rather than symbol-resolved.
A source-only or excluded test/generated artifact reference that is not included in the delivered runtime artifact, where policy is restricted to shipped code.
A call expression with the same method spelling, including getDefaultSharedPreferences, whose resolved owner is not android.preference.PreferenceManager.
protocol: resolve legacy android.preference.PreferenceManager reference or call -> confirm documented deprecation -> emit deprecated-API observation; resolve androidx.preference.PreferenceManager -> replacement-family observation only
